post.caption: The Large Hadron Collider made gold. Turning lead into gold was the dream of medieval alchemists, and in May 2025, scientists at CERN said they had done it. Lead has 82 protons and gold has 79, so a lead nucleus must lose three protons, which happens when lead nuclei nearly miss each other and their strong electromagnetic fields knock protons out. From 2015 to 2018, the collider made about 86 billion gold nuclei, and each one lasted about a microsecond. That is trillions of times too little to make jewelry. All together, they weigh about 29 trillionths of a gram.
